name: JWT Decoder
description: Decode a JSON Web Token's header and payload instantly, and optionally verify an HS256/HS384/HS512 signature against a secret — entirely in your browser.

faq.question: Is it safe to paste a real JWT and secret here?
faq.answer: Every operation runs entirely in your browser using the Web Crypto API — nothing is sent anywhere, and this page works fully offline. That said, treat production secrets carefully in general: prefer testing with a non-production token/secret pair when you can.

faq.question: Why can't this verify RS256/ES256 tokens?
faq.answer: Those are asymmetric algorithms — verifying them needs the issuer's public key, not a shared secret, and safely pasting/handling a public key for arbitrary tokens is a different (and riskier to get subtly wrong) feature than this tool covers. Verification here is limited to the HMAC family (HS256/HS384/HS512), where "verify" is simply "recompute the signature with the same secret and compare" — decoding the header/payload, however, works for every JWT regardless of algorithm, since that part is never encrypted, only base64url-encoded.

faq.question: The signature says invalid but I'm sure the secret is right — why?
faq.answer: Double-check there's no extra whitespace or a trailing newline pasted into the secret field, and that the token's "alg" header actually matches one of HS256/HS384/HS512 (shown in the decoded header) — verifying an RS256 token against a "secret" will always report invalid, since that's not how asymmetric signing works.
